1.why: The reset-verify and reset-complete checks require record.sessionId === session.id, so the token is validated as belonging to the requesting session.

2.why: A reset token is rejected if record.sessionId !== session.id, so the same code does not work for another session/user.

3.why: After password reset the code only invalidates the reset token and changes the current session state; it does not invalidate other existing sessions or rotate session identifiers.

4.why: The app serves HTTPS with certificate and key and redirects HTTP to HTTPS, but the source does not specify or prove use of the latest TLS version.

5.why: Reset tokens are stored in an in-memory Map as plaintext values, and user data is not shown to be encrypted at rest; only the password is bcrypt-hashed.

6.why: There is no real email message; the simulated delivery returns the reset token in the API response and writes it to the visible log, so private reset data is not hidden.

7.why: The code validates identifier format with a regex, safely parses JSON, and enforces password complexity, though it relies more on validation than broad sanitization.

8.why: The only redirect is the HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect to localhost with the requested path/search, so it is same-host but not demonstrably limited to a hospital site.

9.why: No email templates are present, and the simulated notification contains server-generated token text rather than user-supplied HTML or scripts.

10.why: The API returns testToken and mfaCode, and the client-side code logs those values, so private tokens are shown in logs.

11.why: The password is bcrypt-hashed, but the MFA code 482913 is hard-coded in the source and exposed in responses/logs, so secret codes are not securely kept out of the code.

12.why: The fixed MFA code 482913 and demo-account training flow function as default credential/verification material.

13.why: The code enforces attempt limits for reset requests, token verification, and MFA verification using rate-limit counters and token verifyAttempts.

14.why: Although the textual message is generic, the response includes testToken only when the identifier is demo-account, revealing that the account exists.

15.why: Reset codes are generated with crypto.getRandomValues and are long/base64url-encoded, and they are bound to the issuing session, but they are not explicitly bound to a persistent user account.
